contents.support: The local definition specifies a common chart grid and states explicitly that the Sobolev norm does not quotient arbitrary diffeomorphisms.

sources.title: J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations, UC Davis lecture notes, revised 18 June 2014, Chapter 8, “Friedrich symmetric systems”

contents.name: Chapter 8 introduction: positive symmetric systems for boundary-value problems of several PDE types
contents.reason: This chapter introduces a boundary-value theory, while the assigned result is a periodic time-Cauchy comparison with no spatial boundary; its broad applicability claim is not used.

contents.name: Section 8.1, Definition 8.1: smoothness and boundary assumptions for the BVP
contents.reason: The bounded-domain boundary regularity and boundary-matrix hypotheses are absent from the periodic torus problem and do not enter the local finite-slab proof.

contents.name: Section 8.1, Proposition 8.2: Green identity for a symmetric first-order operator
contents.support: The source records the symmetric integration-by-parts identity; the local proof derives its periodic no-boundary version directly on the torus in Step 3.1.

contents.name: Section 8.1, Proposition 8.3: symmetrized energy identity
contents.support: This independent treatment checks the quadratic energy pairing and source term; the new proof supplies the torus calculation and the H^(s-1) commutator bounds.

contents.name: Section 8.1, Definition 8.4: positive symmetric BVP coercivity
contents.reason: This condition is a bulk coercivity inequality for a spatial boundary-value operator, not the positive time matrix A0 required by the assigned Cauchy problem.

contents.name: Section 8.2, Definition 8.5: maximally positive boundary conditions
contents.reason: The assigned problem has periodic spatial topology and no boundary condition; the maximally positive boundary subspaces are not hypotheses of any new item.

contents.name: Section 8.3, Theorem 8.6: coercive estimate for smooth BVP solutions and the adjoint
contents.reason: This theorem is a stationary spatial-boundary coercivity result; the new proof derives a time-evolution estimate and does not import its boundary hypotheses.

contents.name: Section 8.3, Corollary 8.7: uniqueness of smooth solutions under BVP positivity conditions
contents.reason: The corollary depends on the BVP boundary conditions and is not a Cauchy uniqueness theorem; local uniqueness is supplied by the periodic GR14 theorem.

sources.reading_note: The chapter treats positive symmetric boundary-value systems, not the periodic quasilinear Cauchy problem or Einstein equations. Its energy identity is an independent check on the symmetrized quadratic-energy calculation only; all Cauchy, quasilinear, Sobolev and geometric claims are proved from the local carriers.
